Title: Monorepo scaffold
Description: Initialise pnpm workspace with frontend, backend, db, shared, e2e packages. Add tsconfig.base.json (strict), shared flat ESLint (eslint.config.js) + Prettier, .nvmrc (Node 22 LTS), .env.example, .gitignore, .gitattributes (LF), .editorconfig. Root package.json pins packageManager (pnpm) and cross-platform lint/typecheck/format scripts via pnpm -r. Minimal listen-only backend so 0.2's healthcheck has a port. CI ownership stays in 0.3.
Acceptance Criteria: pnpm install works from root; every package (incl. e2e) extends tsconfig.base; pnpm -r lint and pnpm -r typecheck pass on the empty scaffold; .nvmrc + packageManager pin exact versions; .gitattributes forces LF and scripts run on Windows PowerShell; .env.example exists and grows per ticket.
Test Cases: Locally pnpm install, pnpm -r typecheck, pnpm -r lint all green on the empty scaffold. (CI enforcement of the same commands lands in 0.3.)

Title: Docker compose stack
Description: docker-compose.yml orchestrating postgres (Postgres 18), mailpit, backend, frontend + their Dockerfiles under docker/. docker/postgres/init.sql is the SOLE enabler of btree_gist + citext. Base file is CI/prod-like; auto-loaded docker-compose.override.yml adds bind mounts + polling watchers for Windows hot-reload. Credentials/ports from a root .env seeded from .env.example. Prereq: Docker Desktop (WSL2 backend). (When 4.1 lands, a 5th 'worker' service + its health port join this compose file.)
Acceptance Criteria: docker compose up boots all four services on pinned tags; Postgres has btree_gist + citext (from init.sql); Mailpit UI reachable (8025) with SMTP on 1025; the dev override gives backend + frontend hot-reload on file change (polling); each service defines a TCP/port-level healthcheck.
Test Cases: CI smoke test brings up the base file, waits for each service's port healthcheck to pass, and tears down; plus a check that btree_gist is present after up.

Title: CI pipeline skeleton
Description: GitHub Actions on ubuntu-latest, push-to-main + PRs: cached pnpm install -> lint -> typecheck -> unit/integration (Postgres 18 via Testcontainers, no service container) -> coverage. Stages fail fast. Coverage uploaded as a GitHub artifact + job summary; configurable gate with a placeholder threshold (real number set in 7.4). concurrency cancels superseded runs. No e2e stage (added in E7).
Acceptance Criteria: Workflow triggers on push-to-main + PRs; stages run in order and fail fast; integration tests provision Postgres via Testcontainers (no external DB service); coverage report produced, uploaded as artifact + shown in job summary; gate mechanism present and configurable with a placeholder threshold that keeps the empty scaffold green; pnpm store cached across runs.
Test Cases: Pipeline green on the empty scaffold; deliberately breaking a test (or introducing a lint/type error) fails the run and blocks the PR.

Title: DB package + Drizzle + migration tooling
Description: Set up the db package: Drizzle client on node-postgres (pg), drizzle.config.ts, migrate runner (db:generate/db:migrate), seed stub. Schema in db/ as single source with a barrel export. No migrations yet - btree_gist/citext are provided by init.sql (0.2), and the first schema migration is 1.1. Build the Testcontainers helper (template-clone model): boot Postgres 18 once, load the same init.sql, migrate into a template DB, hand each test file a fresh clone.
Acceptance Criteria: db:generate and db:migrate run cleanly against an empty schema; the Testcontainers helper boots Postgres, applies init.sql + all (currently zero) migrations without error, and exposes a fresh cloned DB per test with btree_gist + citext present; pg driver wired; seed stub runs.
Test Cases: The test-db helper boots Postgres via Testcontainers, applies init.sql + all migrations, clones a per-test DB, and asserts btree_gist exists in the clone; db:migrate on an empty schema exits 0.

Title: Users table + migration
Description: Drizzle schema for users: uuid pk (gen_random_uuid()), citext email unique, password_hash (NOT NULL), role pgEnum(user,admin), full_name, created_at/updated_at (timestamptz, UTC). Add citext to init.sql. Partial unique index enforcing a single admin (WHERE role = 'admin'). Create the reusable set_updated_at() trigger function + attach it to users. Data migration inserts the one default admin (admin@physiobook.local, default hash).
Acceptance Criteria: Migration creates users table with case-insensitive unique email, the role enum, and the single-admin partial index; the updated_at trigger fires on update; the default admin row exists after migrate; a second admin insert and a case-differing duplicate email are both rejected.
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers): inserting a second admin row is rejected; Alex@x.com vs alex@x.com treated as duplicate (citext); updated_at changes on update; the seeded admin is present exactly once.

Title: Sessions table + migration
Description: Drizzle schema + migration for sessions (id uuid pk, user_id fk -> users, token_hash, expires_at timestamptz, revoked_at timestamptz null, created_at). Backs the stateless-access + server-side session model used by login, refresh, logout, and the per-request revocation check. token_hash stores the hashed opaque refresh-cookie value (see 1.6). Must land before 1.2 (register auto-login creates a session).
Acceptance Criteria: Migration creates the sessions table with an FK to users and a token_hash column; a session can be created, looked up by id, and marked revoked (revoked_at set); expired vs revoked sessions are distinguishable; a session cannot reference a non-existent user (FK enforced).
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers): insert a session, revoke it, query reflects revoked_at; inserting a session for a missing user is rejected.

Title: Registration endpoint
Description: POST /auth/register - validate {email,password,full_name} with the shared Zod schema (z.strictObject; password min 8 / max 72 bytes for bcrypt). Hash with bcrypt (native, cost 12). Insert with role forced to user; map the unique-email violation -> 409 (insert-and-catch). On success create a session, issue a 15-min access JWT (sub, role, session_id), and set the refresh cookie. Return 201 {user, token}. Rate-limited per client address (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT). AS-BUILT: strictObject rejects any unknown field, so a client-supplied role -> 400 (deliberate deviation from the original 'role ignored' AC; see PROJECT_STRUCTURE §6). Add JWT_SECRET + token TTL to config/env.ts and .env.example.
Acceptance Criteria: Valid payload creates a role=user user + session and returns 201 with the user (no password_hash) plus a valid access JWT and refresh cookie; missing fields, password <8 or >72 bytes, or malformed email -> 400; case-insensitive duplicate email -> 409; a client-supplied role (or any unknown field) -> 400 (strictObject); password stored only as a bcrypt hash; register is rate-limited per client address.
Test Cases: inject(): happy path -> 201 with user + token decoding to {sub, role:user, session_id, exp} and the refresh cookie set; validation failures (missing full_name, short/oversized password, bad email) -> 400; case-differing duplicate email -> 409; body with role:admin (or any unknown field) -> 400; stored hash != plaintext and bcrypt.compare succeeds.

Title: Login endpoint
Description: POST /auth/login - verify {email,password} (citext match; bcrypt compare, with a dummy compare on unknown-user to equalize timing). On success create a session, issue a 15-min access JWT carrying sub/role/session_id, and set the refresh cookie. Return 201 {user, token}. Uniform 401 for wrong password and unknown user. Rate-limited per client address (AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX / AUTH_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_SECONDS); TRUST_PROXY governs what 'client address' means behind a proxy.
Acceptance Criteria: Correct credentials -> a session row is created, a valid access token (with session_id) is returned, and the refresh cookie is set; wrong password or unknown user -> identical 401; token carries role, exp, session_id; login is rate-limited per client address (429 over the limit).
Test Cases: inject(): valid login creates exactly one session and returns a token decoding to the expected claims incl. session_id; wrong password -> 401; unknown user -> 401 (same body); an expired/negative-TTL token fails verification; excess attempts from one address -> 429.

Title: Auth plugin + role guards
Description: Fastify plugin (via fastify-plugin) that on protected routes: verifies the access JWT (signature + exp) using the shared verify util, loads the session by session_id and rejects if revoked or expired (instant-logout check), then decorates request.user = {id, role, sessionId}. Exposes requireAuth (any valid session) and requireRole(...roles) (explicit role set, no hierarchy). Consistent 401/403 error envelope.
Acceptance Criteria: No/invalid/expired token -> 401; valid token but revoked or expired session -> 401; authenticated user whose role isn't in the route's set -> 403; valid token + allowed role -> handler runs with request.user populated; requireRole('user') rejects an admin (403); requireRole('user','admin') admits both.
Test Cases: inject() on sample guarded routes: missing token -> 401; tampered/expired token -> 401; valid-but-revoked session -> 401 (instant-kill); wrong role -> 403; correct role -> 200 with request.user; admin blocked by a user-only guard -> 403; both admitted by a ('user','admin') guard.

Title: Refresh + logout (session-backed)
Description: POST /auth/refresh - read the httpOnly refresh cookie (an OPAQUE random value, not a JWT), verify it against sessions.token_hash, and if the session is live mint a new access token for the same session_id (no rotation; expires_at is an absolute 7-day horizon). POST /auth/logout (requireAuth, authenticated by the access token) stamps sessions.revoked_at and clears the cookie. Refresh has its own wider rate-limit bucket (REFRESH_RATE_LIMIT_MAX). AS-BUILT: no JWT_REFRESH_SECRET - the cookie is opaque so there is nothing to sign (PROJECT_STRUCTURE §10); REFRESH_TTL_SECONDS exists from 1.3. Wire @fastify/cookie.
Acceptance Criteria: Valid refresh cookie -> new access token (200); missing/expired/revoked session -> 401; logout revokes the session and clears the cookie; after logout, both refresh and any live access token are rejected (via the 1.4 guard); the refresh cookie is an opaque value verified against sessions.token_hash (no signing secret); refresh has its own rate-limit bucket.
Test Cases: inject(): valid cookie -> new access token; no cookie -> 401; after logout, a still-unexpired access token is rejected by a guarded route (instant-kill proof); refresh on a revoked session -> 401.

Title: Frontend auth flow
Description: Login + register forms validated with the shared Zod schemas. AuthProvider/useAuth holding the in-memory access token + user. Typed fetch wrapper: attaches Bearer, and on 401 runs a single-flight /auth/refresh then retries; on refresh failure, clears state -> /login. Silent refresh on app load (rehydrate from the httpOnly cookie) behind an auth-loading gate so guarded routes don't flash to login. Protected routes redirect unauthenticated users to /login (return-to preserved) and redirect wrong-role users to their own area. Role-based nav. Register auto-logs-in into the user area; admin logs in via the same form and lands in the admin area. Logout calls /auth/logout, clears the token, redirects.
Acceptance Criteria: User can register (and is immediately logged in) and log in; admin logs in via the same form and reaches the admin area; the access token is attached to requests, and an expired one triggers a single silent refresh so the original request still succeeds; on reload the session is restored with no flash to login (invalid cookie -> logged out); unauthenticated access to a guarded route redirects to /login with return-to; wrong-role access redirects to the user's own area; nav renders per role; logout returns the app to a logged-out state.
Test Cases: RTL: register/login validation states (shared schemas); the auth-loading gate shows a spinner then content; wrong-role redirect. RTL with a mocked api: concurrent 401s fire /auth/refresh exactly once then retry (single-flight). Playwright E2E: register -> land in user area (auto-login) -> reload stays logged in -> logout -> guarded route redirects to login; plus admin login -> admin area.

Title: GET /auth/me (identity endpoint)
Description: GET /auth/me (requireAuth) - reads the users row named by the validated access token and returns publicUserSchema (the same shape register/login nest under 'user'). Enables the frontend's on-load rehydration (refresh -> me: a credential, then an identity), since /auth/refresh answers {token} alone. Re-reads the row (email/full_name/role are not claims); a missing row -> 401 (account deleted mid-request), not 404. AS-BUILT: shipped in E1.5, not in the original backlog.
Acceptance Criteria: Guarded by requireAuth; returns the caller's public profile read from the DB; unauthenticated -> 401; missing user row -> 401 (not 404).
Test Cases: inject(): valid token -> public profile; no/invalid/expired token -> 401; deleted-user row -> 401.

Title: practice_settings singleton
Description: Table + migration for singleton practice_settings: id (pk, CHECK id=1), timezone (IANA), slot_duration_minutes (kept, seeded 60, not editable - slots stay fixed 1h per domain rule), reminder_lead_hours, cancellation_cutoff_hours, created_at/updated_at (timestamptz + set_updated_at trigger). Seed the default row. GET /settings (any authenticated user) returns the policy fields; PUT /settings (admin only) updates the editable ones. Validate with a shared Zod schema (valid IANA tz; reminder_lead_hours > 0; cancellation_cutoff_hours >= 0). AS-BUILT: PUT validates timezone against Intl.supportedValuesOf('timeZone') plus an explicit allowance for 'UTC' (the one canonical name the ECMA-402 list omits, and the seed default). A client-supplied slot_duration_minutes -> 400 (strictObject rejects it as an unknown field, same deliberate deviation from a literal 'ignored' AC as ticket 1.2 - see BACKEND_DEV.md §2 / PROJECT_STRUCTURE.md §6).
Acceptance Criteria: Exactly one settings row (CHECK id=1 + pk) - a second is rejected; defaults seeded to match the domain rules (reminder 24, cutoff 24, slot 60); any authenticated user can read the policy fields; only admin can update (non-admin PUT -> 403); slot_duration_minutes is not editable; invalid timezone or out-of-range values -> 400; the updated_at trigger fires on update.
Test Cases: Integration: a second settings row is rejected. inject(): a user can GET the policy fields; user PUT -> 403; admin PUT valid -> 200 and persists; admin PUT with a bad timezone / negative cutoff -> 400; an attempt to change slot_duration_minutes -> 400 (rejected as an unknown field, not silently ignored; see AS-BUILT note). updated_at changes on update.

Title: Business hours CRUD (admin)
Description: business_hours table (id, day_of_week 0-6 [0=Sun], open/close as TIME wall-clock in the practice tz). Admin edits via PUT /business-hours - whole-week bulk replace: client sends all windows, server validates then swaps them in a transaction. Split shifts allowed (multiple windows/day). Zod validation: day_of_week 0-6, close>open per window, no overlapping windows within a day; open/close may be any time (not restricted to the hour). GET /business-hours readable by any authenticated user. Changing hours does not retroactively affect existing appointments.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin bulk-replaces the weekly windows atomically - any validation error rejects the whole replace with no partial write; close<=open, day_of_week out of 0-6, and overlapping same-day windows are all rejected; non-overlapping split shifts are accepted; any authenticated user can read the effective weekly hours; non-admin PUT -> 403.
Test Cases: inject(): valid bulk replace persists all windows; close<=open rejected; day out of range rejected; overlapping same-day windows rejected (replace fails atomically, prior config intact); split shift (09:00-12:00 + 14:00-18:00) accepted; non-admin PUT -> 403; user GET -> 200.

Title: Slot generation service + GET /slots
Description: Service computing bookable on-the-hour 1h slots for a practitioner over a practice-tz date range (capped 62 days). A slot [H:00,H+1:00) is bookable iff fully contained in an open business_hours window, not overlapping any active calendar_blocks row (appointment or time-off), and start > now (injectable clock). Computed with Luxon in the practice timezone, converting local wall-clock hours to UTC instants. DST: spring-forward nonexistent hour yields no slot; fall-back repeated hour yields a single slot at the earlier UTC offset. Exposes a shared isSlotBookable(start) helper (reused by 3.2) and a GET /slots endpoint (authenticated; query = date range in practice-tz days, capped 62) returning UTC slot instants for the frontend (2.4 preview, 3.5 picker). Scoped by practitioner_id. (5.3 reuses this grid; factor it to parameterize which blocks to subtract and whether to include past.)
Acceptance Criteria: Returns correct open slots for a range; excludes taken slots and time-off; excludes past slots; emits on-the-hour slots each fully inside an open window (e.g. 09:30-17:30 -> 10:00..16:00); spring-forward skipped hour absent; fall-back repeated hour yields exactly one slot; over-cap ranges rejected. GET /slots returns bookable slots for a valid range to authenticated users; invalid/over-cap range -> 400.
Test Cases: Fixed-clock unit tests: normal week; containment for a 09:30-17:30 window; fully-booked day -> no slots; time-off excluded; spring-forward day -> skipped hour absent; fall-back day -> single slot for the repeated hour; past slots excluded relative to injected now. Property test: generated slots are on-the-hour, mutually non-overlapping, and none overlap active blocks or fall outside business hours. inject(): GET /slots returns expected open slots for a range; over-cap range -> 400.

Title: Admin availability UI (+ settings)
Description: Admin availability screen. A weekly-grid editor for business hours (7 days, add/remove windows per day for split shifts, 15-min time inputs); Save issues 2.2's whole-week PUT. Inline validation mirrors the shared Zod rules (close>open, no same-day overlaps, valid day) with a form-level overlap message and a dirty-state guard. Includes a practice-settings section (timezone via IANA picker, reminder_lead_hours, cancellation_cutoff_hours) saved via PUT /settings. A live slot-preview panel calls the 2.3 service to show resulting bookable slots. Admin-only route.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin can edit and save both business hours (bulk replace) and practice settings; validation is surfaced inline and overlaps/invalid ranges are blocked before save; after saving, the slot preview reflects the new hours and timezone; non-admin cannot reach the screen.
Test Cases: RTL: add/remove windows; close<=open and same-day overlap show inline errors; dirty-guard on navigate-away; settings form rejects an invalid timezone. Playwright: edit hours + timezone -> save -> slot preview/booking list updates.

Title: calendar_blocks + appointments + EXCLUDE constraint
Description: Migration creating calendar_blocks (id uuid pk, practitioner_id FK->users(id), kind pgEnum(appointment,time_off), period tstzrange with '[)' bounds in UTC, status pgEnum(active,cancelled,cancelled_by_admin) default active, created_at/updated_at + set_updated_at trigger) with the scoped EXCLUDE USING gist (practitioner_id WITH =, period WITH &&) WHERE status='active'. CHECK (whole-hour-offset assumption documented): for kind='appointment', lower(period) on the UTC hour and upper-lower = 1 hour; time_off exempt (arbitrary range, lower<upper). appointments table (id uuid pk, block_id unique FK->calendar_blocks, user_id FK->users) 1:1 with an appointment block; status lives on the block. Seed uses the admin user as practitioner. (5.1 adds a nullable note column used by time-off.)
Acceptance Criteria: EXCLUDE present and active - two overlapping active blocks: second rejected at the DB; adjacent blocks ('[)' bounds) do not conflict; cancelled/cancelled_by_admin blocks don't block; appointment blocks must start on the UTC hour and be exactly 1h (off-hour or non-1h rejected); time_off arbitrary ranges allowed; appointment is 1:1 with its block and requires a valid user_id.
Test Cases: Testcontainers: two overlapping active inserts -> second rejected; adjacent [10,11)+[11,12) both accepted (no false conflict); a cancelled block does not block a new overlapping active block; off-hour (10:30) and non-1h (2h) appointments rejected; arbitrary-range time_off accepted; appointment requires unique block_id + valid user_id.

Title: Book appointment endpoint
Description: POST /appointments (requireRole('user')). Payload {start} (UTC ISO); end = start+1h; user_id from the token; practitioner_id = seeded physio. Validate via the shared isSlotBookable(start) helper (also used by 2.3): on-the-hour, within business hours, not past, within the 62-day window - NO pre-check for freeness. Insert calendar_block + appointment in one transaction; rely on the DB EXCLUDE for freeness, catching the exclusion violation -> clean 409 'slot taken' with full rollback. Return 201 with the created appointment. (4.3 later hooks reminder-job scheduling into this booking flow.)
Acceptance Criteria: Valid free slot -> 201; taken slot -> 409 'slot taken'; out-of-hours/off-hour/past/beyond-window -> 422; malformed body -> 400; booking is for the authenticated user (user_id from token, not payload); admin (role=admin) -> 403; on conflict the transaction rolls back fully with no orphan block.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: happy path -> 201; taken slot -> 409; out-of-hours / off-hour / past -> 422; conflict rolls back fully (no orphan calendar_block); admin -> 403; a payload trying to spoof another user_id still books for the token's user.

Title: Concurrent booking race test (headline)
Description: The headline concurrency proof. Seed N=20 distinct patients; fire Promise.all of 20 concurrent POST /appointments (.inject()) at one slot against real Postgres (Testcontainers, pool >= N); assert exactly one 201, nineteen clean 409s, zero 500s/deadlocks, and exactly one active appointment/block in the DB. Repeat ~10 iterations. Plus a same-user double-submit variant (one user, N concurrent identical requests) -> exactly one booking. Outcome deterministic regardless of which request wins.
Acceptance Criteria: Exactly one 201, all others 409 (never 500/deadlock); DB holds exactly one active appointment for the slot with no orphan/partial blocks; the same-user concurrent double-submit yields exactly one booking; stable across repeated iterations.
Test Cases: Testcontainers + Promise.all of N .inject() POSTs (pool >= N): assert status counts (1x201, N-1x409, 0x500) and final DB state; repeat 10x. Same-user variant -> one 201, rest 409, one booking.

Title: Cancel appointment (24h rule)
Description: DELETE /appointments/:id (requireRole('user')). User cancels their own active appointment only if now <= start - cancellation_cutoff_hours (compared on UTC instants, injectable clock). Flips the block status -> cancelled, freeing the slot (partial EXCLUDE). Returns 200 with the cancelled appointment. Note: when reminders (4.3) land, user-cancel must also cancel the pending reminder job.
Acceptance Criteria: Cancel at >cutoff -> 200 and the slot becomes re-bookable; within cutoff -> 422; another user's appointment -> 403; non-existent -> 404; already-cancelled -> 409; only active appointments are cancellable.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers (fixed clock): cancel at 25h -> 200, slot re-bookable after; at 23h -> 422; cross-user -> 403; non-existent id -> 404; second cancel of the same appointment -> 409.

Title: Booking UI (slot picker)
Description: User booking page (requireRole('user') route). Fetches bookable slots from GET /slots (2.3) for the selected date/range, rendered in the practice timezone (tz label) with date navigation; shows only open slots with an empty-state when none. Click a slot -> confirm dialog (date/time in practice tz) -> POST /appointments with optimistic feedback: on 201 confirm + update list; on 409 revert, show 'slot just taken', and refetch. Graceful two-tab race handling.
Acceptance Criteria: User sees only open slots in practice tz; booking updates the list; 409 handled gracefully with a refetch; confirm dialog precedes booking; empty-state when no slots; page is user-only.
Test Cases: RTL: picker rendering + absent taken slots; confirm-dialog flow; 409 revert + message (mocked api). Playwright: book end-to-end; two-tab race (second tab sees 'slot taken').

Title: pg-boss integration + worker
Description: Wire pg-boss on the shared Postgres (pg-boss manages its own schema on start()). Separate jobs/worker.ts process as its own compose service (5th service), exposing a tiny /health HTTP endpoint (reports pg-boss connected) for the compose healthcheck. Shared pg-boss config module: the API enqueues (send/schedule), the worker consumes (work). Graceful SIGTERM -> boss.stop(). At 4.1 only a no-op test handler.
Acceptance Criteria: pg-boss schema created on start; the worker service boots, registers handlers, and its /health reports healthy; a no-op job enqueued by the API is processed by the worker exactly once; the worker shuts down gracefully on SIGTERM.
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers, in-process pg-boss): enqueue a no-op job -> the worker handler processes it exactly once.

Title: Email transport + Mailpit
Description: mailer.ts over nodemailer SMTP: Mailpit (:1025) in dev/test, real SMTP creds in prod - swappable by env (MAIL_* + MAIL_FROM in config/env.ts + .env.example). Messages built by typed template functions returning {subject, text, html} (minimal inline HTML). Test harness gains a Mailpit Testcontainer helper (send via SMTP :1025, assert via the :8025 HTTP API).
Acceptance Criteria: Mail sent in dev/test lands in Mailpit; transport swappable by env; each mail has a templated subject + text/html; missing mail config fails fast at boot.
Test Cases: Integration (Mailpit Testcontainer): send a templated mail -> assert it appears via Mailpit's HTTP API with the expected subject/recipient.

Title: Schedule + send 24h reminders
Description: notification_log(dedupe_key UNIQUE, type, recipient, sent_at) for exactly-once. On booking (hook into 3.2), schedule a pg-boss job at start - reminder_lead_hours; skip if booked inside the window. At fire time the handler: (1) self-guards - skips if the appointment is no longer active; (2) sends the user's individual reminder (claim reminder:user:{apptId}); (3) if the appointment is the earliest active appointment of its contiguous run, sends one grouped admin mail counting the active run with singular/plural wording + a list, claiming reminder:admin-run:{runStartInstant}. Rendered in practice tz. Changing reminder_lead_hours later does not reschedule existing jobs. (7.3 requires an env-guarded clock-advance/due-job trigger, enabled only under the E2E flag.)
Acceptance Criteria: Reminder fires ~lead before; an active appointment -> the user gets an individual mail; the run's earliest active appointment triggers exactly one grouped admin mail counting adjacent active appointments (singular vs 'N appointments starting at HH:MM' + list); a cancelled appointment produces no mail and is excluded from the admin count; no reminder scheduled when booked inside the window; a retried job yields one log row / one mail.
Test Cases: Fake clock, Testcontainers + Mailpit: single appt -> user mail + admin mail (count 1, singular); three consecutive -> one grouped admin mail (count 3, plural, listed) + three user mails; cancel one of the run pre-fire -> admin count excludes it; cancel the run-start -> the next active appt sends the grouped mail; job run twice -> one log row / one mail; booked <lead out -> no reminder; non-consecutive appts -> separate admin mails.

Title: Cancellation notifications
Description: On admin hard-cancel (5.2), enqueue a send-cancellation pg-boss job; the worker sends the affected user a cancellation email via mailer (retry on failure), deduped via notification_log (cancellation:{apptId}). Content: the appointment's date/time (practice tz), cancelled by the clinic. The reminder is already suppressed by 4.3's self-guard (no active job cancellation needed). Only admin hard-cancel triggers this.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin hard-cancel -> the user receives exactly one cancellation email (deduped); the appointment's reminder does not fire (self-guarded); a transient send failure is retried without duplicating.
Test Cases: Integration (Testcontainers + Mailpit): admin cancel -> user cancellation mail in Mailpit; the pending reminder does not fire after cancel; re-running the job -> still one mail.

Title: Book time off (+ remove, overlap error)
Description: POST /time-off (requireRole('admin')) - insert a time_off block over an arbitrary range {start,end} (UTC, start<end, optional note) for the physio. Rely on the DB EXCLUDE; on an exclusion violation, query the overlapping active blocks and return a 409 listing them. DELETE /time-off/:id - flip a time_off block to cancelled, freeing those slots. Active time-off is excluded from bookable slots by 2.3.
Acceptance Criteria: Free range -> 201; a range overlapping an active appointment or existing time-off -> 409 listing the conflicting block(s); booked time-off hidden from bookable slots; DELETE cancels a time-off block and those slots become bookable again; non-admin -> 403; non-existent/already-cancelled handled (404/409).
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: free range -> 201; overlap with an appointment -> 409 with the conflict listed; overlap with existing time-off -> 409; slots exclude the time-off afterwards; DELETE frees the slots; non-admin -> 403.

Title: Hard-cancel any appointment
Description: POST /admin/appointments/:id/cancel (requireRole('admin')) - cancels any future active appointment regardless of the 24h rule; sets status='cancelled_by_admin', freeing the slot; enqueues the 4.4 send-cancellation job. The 4.3 reminder self-guards (no explicit job cancel).
Acceptance Criteria: Admin cancels any future active appointment at any time -> 200, slot re-bookable, cancellation job enqueued; a past appointment -> 422 (already started); already-cancelled -> 409; non-existent -> 404; non-admin -> 403.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: admin cancels a same-day (future) appt -> 200, slot re-bookable, cancellation job enqueued; non-admin -> 403; past appointment -> 422; already-cancelled -> 409.

Title: Workload dashboard endpoint
Description: GET /admin/workload?from&to&granularity=day|week (requireRole('admin')). Reuses 2.3's factored slot-grid: capacity = business-hours slots minus time-off (past included, appointments not subtracted); booked = active appointments; open = capacity - booked. Aggregated by practice-tz day or ISO (Mon-start) week; range capped 92 days; past + future allowed. Output [{period, capacity, booked, open}].
Acceptance Criteria: Correct capacity/booked/open per period; respects business hours and time-off; only active appointments count as booked; empty day -> all-open; full day -> all-busy; a day fully covered by time-off -> capacity 0; day and ISO-week granularity; non-admin -> 403.
Test Cases: Integration: seeded data yields expected aggregates; empty day all-open; full day all-busy; time-off reduces capacity; week granularity groups Mon-Sun; non-admin -> 403.

Title: List all appointments (admin)
Description: GET /admin/appointments (requireRole('admin')) - lists appointments across all patients with start/end (joined from the block), patient name, and status; date-range + status filters (default: upcoming active); ordered by start.
Acceptance Criteria: Returns all patients' appointments for the range (not just the caller's); includes patient + status; default = upcoming active, filterable to past/cancelled; non-admin -> 403.
Test Cases: inject()+Testcontainers: returns appointments across users; default shows upcoming active; filter reveals past/cancelled; correct ordering; non-admin -> 403.

Title: Admin dashboard UI
Description: Admin-only dashboard. Appointments list from GET /admin/appointments (upcoming active default, past/cancelled filter) with per-row hard-cancel (confirm -> 5.2). Workload chart (Recharts) from GET /admin/workload with a day/week toggle. Time-off section: range-picker to book (5.1, surfacing the 409 overlap conflicts) + a list of existing time-off with remove (DELETE). Errors inline; times in practice tz.
Acceptance Criteria: Admin sees all appointments (upcoming default, filterable) and the workload chart; can book time off (overlap error surfaced), remove it, and hard-cancel from the list; non-admin cannot reach the screen.
Test Cases: RTL: appointments list + filter; workload chart render; time-off form validation + overlap error; hard-cancel confirm. Playwright: book time off (incl. overlap error), remove time off, hard-cancel flow.

Title: List user appointments endpoint
Description: GET /appointments/me (requireRole('user')) - returns the caller's own appointments grouped {upcoming, past}: upcoming soonest-first, past most-recent-first, each {id, start, end, status} in UTC (active + cancelled). Each upcoming appointment includes a server-computed canCancel flag + cancellableUntil (from cancellation_cutoff_hours), matching 3.4's enforcement. Past capped/paginated (limit); user_id from the token; excludes other users'.
Acceptance Criteria: Returns only the caller's appointments, grouped upcoming/past with correct ordering; includes status (active + cancelled); each upcoming carries canCancel/cancellableUntil consistent with 3.4; excludes others'; unauthenticated -> 401.
Test Cases: inject(): returns own only (not others'); upcoming soonest-first, past most-recent-first; cancelled appear with status; canCancel true outside cutoff and false within; unauthenticated -> 401.

Title: User panel UI + nearest-appointment countdown
Description: User panel (requireRole('user') route). Lists appointments from GET /appointments/me (grouped upcoming/past, cancelled shown with status), times in practice tz. Live countdown to the soonest upcoming appointment (ticks; rolls to the next when it passes). Per-upcoming cancel gated by the server's canCancel: disabled within the cutoff with an explanation, else DELETE /appointments/:id (3.4) -> refetch; a 422 (lost race) surfaces a message. Empty-state with a link to book.
Acceptance Criteria: Panel shows upcoming + past (cancelled tagged); the countdown ticks to the nearest upcoming and advances when it passes; cancel is disabled within the cutoff with an explanation (driven by canCancel); an eligible cancel succeeds and updates the list; empty-state links to booking.
Test Cases: RTL: countdown with fake timers; disabled-cancel state (canCancel=false) + explanation; eligible cancel flow (mocked api) + refetch; empty-state. Playwright: view panel + cancel an eligible appointment.

Title: E2E: full booking journey (+ CI e2e stage)
Description: Playwright journey: register (auto-login) -> book a slot >24h out -> see it in the panel -> cancel (eligible); plus a logout/login assertion. Builds the CI e2e stage deferred from 0.3: GitHub Actions boots the docker-compose stack, waits for healthchecks, migrates, runs a dedicated e2e seed/fixtures (settings + business hours + admin so bookable slots exist), runs Playwright against the compose frontend, uploads traces on failure, tears down. Fresh DB per CI run (empty volume + reseed).
Acceptance Criteria: The full journey passes against the docker-compose stack; the e2e stage runs in CI on a freshly seeded stack; the dedicated e2e seed produces a known bookable schedule; traces uploaded on failure.
Test Cases: Playwright green in CI against compose: register -> book -> panel -> cancel, plus logout/login.

Title: E2E: two-user slot race
Description: Playwright: two browser contexts (two seeded patients) poised on the same slot; clicks fired together (Promise.all at the confirm step). One books; the other sees a graceful 'slot taken' and the slot disappears (refetch). Asserts both UI outcomes and, via a direct Postgres count, exactly one active appointment. Runs on the 7.1 compose stack/seed.
Acceptance Criteria: Exactly one context books; the other gets a clear 'slot taken' message; a direct DB count confirms exactly one active appointment; no partial state.
Test Cases: Two contexts -> one success + one conflict UI; direct DB count = 1 active appointment.

Title: E2E: notification flows via Mailpit
Description: Playwright + compose Mailpit. An env-guarded test-only hook (enabled only under an E2E flag, absent in prod) advances the clock / fires due reminder jobs so reminders trigger without real waiting. Scenarios: single-appointment reminder (user mail); grouped-admin reminder (book consecutive slots -> one counted admin mail); admin hard-cancel -> cancellation email. Asserts via the Mailpit HTTP API (subject, recipient, grouped count/list).
Acceptance Criteria: Individual + grouped-admin reminders (correct count) and the cancellation email appear in Mailpit for the scripted scenarios; the trigger hook is disabled outside E2E.
Test Cases: Playwright drives each flow, advances time via the guarded hook, asserts Mailpit contents (recipients, grouped admin count).

Title: Coverage gate + timezone/DST suite
Description: Flip 0.3's placeholder coverage gate to a real enforced threshold: global 90% lines + branches (excluding migrations/config/generated), blocking merges below it in CI. Add a consolidated Luxon timezone/DST suite spanning booking (3.2), slot generation (2.3), and reminders (4.3): spring-forward and fall-back transitions (Europe/Warsaw, fixed known dates).
Acceptance Criteria: The gate blocks merges below 90% lines + branches; excluded paths (migrations/config/generated) not counted; the DST suite passes for both spring-forward and fall-back across booking, slots, and reminders.
Test Cases: CI fails below threshold (verified via a deliberate uncovered path); DST tests green for both transitions.
